meta.title: Marmoria
meta.description: Govern a Roman city: lay out roads and districts, bring in water, bread, workshops and shows, and watch tents grow into insulae.
meta.titre_seo: Marmoria: build a Roman city, free city-building game
meta.description_seo: Build a Roman city: roads, water, farms, workshops, temples and shows. Your people move up from tents to grand insulae. Free management game for ages 13+.
meta.presentation: Marmoria is a management game where you govern a Roman city seen from above, in 3D. You lay out the roads and districts, then settlers come in along the Road to Rome and pitch their tents. Everything happens in the streets: market sellers, prefects, priests, teachers, doctors and performers make their rounds, and every house they serve grows, from a tent to a grand insula. Farms, fishing wharves, quarries and workshops supply food, pottery, furniture and oil, which caravans and ships trade with the cities of the Empire. You have to keep an eye on fire, wear and tear on buildings, jobs, taxes and health, keep five gods happy and answer the emperor's requests. The campaign has 17 maps; in this version, five missions, from Ostia to Massalia, and free build are playable.
meta.regles: Goal: meet the mission's targets: population, then culture, prosperity, peace and the emperor's favour. With a mouse, pick a building in the left menu, then click or drag on the map; right-click for info, scroll wheel to zoom, arrow keys to move around, R to rotate the view, P or Esc to pause. On a touch screen, swipe, then tap Confirm; two fingers pan and zoom, and a long press shows info. Each mission earns up to 3 stars: winning, getting no bailout from the emperor, and winning before the target date. An empty, broke city is lost, and so is a governor the emperor keeps in disgrace for too long.
meta.competences: city planning, budget management, anticipating risks, reading data
meta.jaquette_alt: Two marble temples, one white and one pink, among gardens, shacks, tents and a fountain in the sun

textes.bat.grenier.aide: Holds up to 24 loads of food for the markets.
textes.bat.marche.aide: Its buyer goes to the granary or warehouse, and its seller stocks up the houses she passes.
textes.bat.temple_ceres.aide: Its priest gives the houses he passes access to Ceres, goddess of the harvest.
textes.bat.theatre.aide: When an actor arrives, it puts on a 32-day show: its performers bring 15 entertainment points.
textes.bat.colonie_acteurs.aide: Trains actors and sends them to the nearest theater that needs one.
textes.bat.forum.aide: Its tax collector registers houses: only registered houses pay taxes.
textes.bat.prefecture.aide: Its prefect lowers fire risk and rushes to put out fires within 15 tiles.
textes.bat.ingenieur.aide: Its engineer repairs the buildings he passes and prevents collapses.
textes.bat.ruines.aide: What's left after a fire. Clear them to rebuild.
textes.bat.gravats.aide: What's left after a collapse. Clear it to rebuild.
textes.bat.incendie.aide: Fire can spread to nearby buildings. A prefect puts it out in 2 days.
textes.cause.sansPreneur: storage full, nowhere to send it (granary, warehouse or workshop)

textes.info.bientot: All set: the house is about to grow.

textes.marcheur.emigrant.aide: Unhappy with the city and leaving the map.
textes.marcheur.sansabri.aide: Their house burned down or shrank: they're looking for a new home, or else they'll leave.
textes.marcheur.livreur.aide: Pushes a cart holding one load of goods.
textes.marcheur.acheteuse.aide: Brings one load of food from the granary back to the market.
textes.marcheur.vendeuse.aide: Stocks up the houses she passes, with up to 4 months of food.
textes.marcheur.prefet.aide: Lowers the fire risk of the buildings he passes and puts out fires.
textes.marcheur.percepteur.aide: Registers houses for taxes for 48 days.
textes.marcheur.pretre.aide: Gives the houses he passes access to his temple's god.
textes.marcheur.acteur.aide: Goes from the actors' colony to the theater for a new show.
textes.marcheur.comedien.aide: Brings the theater's show to the houses he passes.
textes.terrain.prairieAide: The only land where farms can go.
textes.terrain.eauAide: A reservoir built on the shore fills up by itself.
textes.terrain.romeAide: Immigrants and emigrants pass through here. It can't be removed.
textes.conseil.immigrationArretee: Mood is too low: nobody wants to move in anymore.
textes.calque.eauAide: Light blue: well water. Dark blue: fountain water. The columns show the water at each house.
textes.calque.feuAide: The taller and redder the column, the bigger the fire threat. Only prefects stay visible.
textes.calque.dommagesAide: The taller and redder the column, the more likely the building is to collapse. Only engineers stay visible.
textes.calque.stocksAide: Granaries, markets and warehouses: the taller and greener the column, the fuller they are; red means almost empty. Only cart pushers, haulers, buyers and sellers stay visible.
textes.tuto.ostie.1: Open “Housing” and lay out 10 housing tiles within 2 tiles of the Road to Rome.
textes.tuto.ostie.2: Immigrants come in by the Road to Rome. Wait until you have 24 residents (you can speed up time with +).
textes.tuto.ostie.3: The tents are thirsty: open “Water” and place 2 wells in the middle of your housing.
textes.tuto.ostie.4: With water, a small tent becomes a large tent. Wait until you have 6.
textes.tuto.ostie.5: Your people need bread: place a wheat farm on fertile meadow (the light green), near a road.
textes.tuto.ostie.6: The wheat goes to a granary: build one connected to the farm by road.
textes.tuto.ostie.7: Build a market near the houses: its buyer will go to the granary, and its seller will feed the houses.
textes.tuto.ostie.8: Once fed, tents turn into shacks. Grow 5 houses into small shacks (long-press a house to see what it's missing).
textes.tuto.ostie.9: Final goal: reach 150 residents. Add housing, wells and a 2nd market if needed.
textes.tuto.pompei.1: Tents catch fire easily: open “Security” and build a prefecture along a road.
textes.tuto.pompei.2: Without upkeep, buildings collapse: build an engineer's post.
textes.tuto.pompei.3: To collect taxes, build a forum: its tax collector registers the houses he passes.
textes.tuto.pompei.4: Build a small temple of Ceres near the shacks. Grow 8 houses into large shacks.
textes.tuto.pompei.5: Place a reservoir on the riverbank, connect it by aqueduct to a reservoir in town, then add fountains around it. Grow 8 houses into small hovels.
textes.tuto.pompei.6: Build an actors' colony and a theater: their shows will grow 8 houses into large hovels.
textes.tuto.pompei.7: Final goal: reach 600 residents. Keep an eye on mood and taxes in the Government panel.
textes.tuto.fini: Tutorial complete: the city is yours.

textes.mission.ostie.intro: Rome's port needs workers. On this empty coast, welcome your first settlers: housing, water, bread. The tutorial guides you step by step.
textes.mission.pompei.intro: At the foot of the volcano, the city grows fast and burns just as fast. Protect it from fires and collapses, collect taxes, and give it a temple, fountains and a theater.
textes.briefing.etoiles: 1 star for winning, 1 for getting no help from the emperor, 1 if you win in {mois} months or less.

textes.mission.ravenne.intro: On the edge of the Adriatic lagoons, Ravenna must become a city of craftsmen. Get its workshops going, sell your pottery to the nearby cities and answer the emperor's requests.
textes.mission.narbo.intro: Narbo, the young colony of southern Gaul, opens onto the sea. Forge weapons, build a trade quay and send your ships to Hispania and Ostia.
textes.mission.massalia.intro: Massalia, the great Greek port allied to Rome. Fish, press olive oil, sell it across the Empire and turn the city into a rich and cultured one.
